chixoy-rio-negro.conditions_add: The Bank's 1978 appraisal of the Chixoy Power Project sets out the agreements reached with the Government and the state electricity utility INDE for the US$72 million loan. INDE had to furnish the Bank by 31 December 1979 a programme to compensate adequately and, if necessary, resettle the roughly 1,500 residents of the area to be flooded by the Chixoy reservoir, and to present an erosion control programme for the reservoir watershed by the same date, which the Government had to put into effect by 30 June 1980. The Government also had to keep power sector revenues sufficient to finance sector investment from internally generated funds at no less than 13 percent in 1978, 16 percent in 1979 and 18 percent thereafter until the Aguacapa project was completed, and to achieve an 8 percent rate of return on annually valued assets after that; power rates had to be adjusted automatically to cover higher fuel prices, and could not be reduced without the Bank's agreement before the project was completed (World Bank, Staff Appraisal Report, 1978). The only condition of loan effectiveness the appraisal gives is the amendment of the subsidiary contract between the Government, INDE and the Guatemala City utility.

why.safeguard: compensate adequately and, if necessary, resettle the roughly 1,500 residents of the area to be flooded
why.prices: power rates had to be adjusted automatically to cover higher fuel prices
why.fincov: achieve an 8 percent rate of return on annually valued assets

kainji-dam.conditions_add: The Bank's 1964 appraisal records that, as a condition of effectiveness of the Bank loan, at least US$45 million equivalent of other foreign loans had to be signed on terms acceptable to the Bank. The Niger Dams Authority had to earn revenues giving at least an 8 percent return on its average net fixed assets in operation, could take on no debt during construction without the Bank's consent and from 1 January 1969 only if net revenue covered maximum future annual debt service 1.5 times, had to be audited each year by independent public accountants acceptable to the Bank, and could not have a chief executive whose qualifications the Bank had not accepted. No other generating plant for the interconnected system could be built before Kainji was fully developed without the Bank's approval, and the Government agreed to provide any additional funds necessary to complete the project (World Bank, Staff Appraisal Report, Kainji Multipurpose Project, 1964). The appraisal's list of covenants carries no Bank covenant on resettlement: the report notes "the displacement of some 140,000 persons" and the total submergence of the town of Bussa, and a cost estimate providing funds for compensation and resettlement of an existing population of about 40,000, but attaches no obligation about how that was to be done.

why.fincov: revenues giving at least an 8 percent return on its average net fixed assets in operation
why.admin: could not have a chief executive whose qualifications the Bank had not accepted

pak-mun.conditions_add: The Bank's 1991 appraisal of Thailand's Third Power System Development Project, which finances Pak Mun as one of its components, sets out what the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand was to do. EGAT would implement a plan, satisfactory to the Bank, for the resettlement and rehabilitation of people involuntarily resettled by the subproject, with minimum entitlements of at least 0.08 hectares of land for home plots and 1.6 hectares of land for farm plots, or reconstruction of their existing houses on backfilled ground near the original locations; a fisheries development plan, satisfactory to the Bank, including a fisheries conservation unit, fish migration studies and construction and monitoring of a fish ladder for migratory fish; a plan, satisfactory to the Bank, for the prevention, control and mitigation of endemic diseases; and a subproject site management plan, satisfactory to the Bank, covering construction runoff, spoil areas, archaeological sites and farmland. EGAT also agreed to appoint a board of three consultants to review the design and construction of the project and to make the environmental impact assessment, mitigation and resettlement reports available for public inspection at its offices (World Bank, Staff Appraisal Report, 1991).

jakarta-water-1997.conditions_add: The appraisal of the Second Jabotabek Urban Development Project, which onlent about US$92 million of the US$190 million loan to the Jakarta water enterprise PDAM Jaya, made two things conditions of loan effectiveness: execution of satisfactory subsidiary loan agreements between the government and DKI Jakarta, PDAM Jaya and PDAM Tangerang, and establishment of a separate division in the project coordination office JUPCO with its key staff (division manager, financial accountant and monitoring officer) appointed. The agreements for PDAM Jaya set financial targets of about a 30 percent contribution to the investment programme through net internal cash generation, debt capped at 70 percent of debt plus equity and debt service coverage of at least 1.5, and required DKI Jakarta to review and adjust PDAM Jaya's tariffs every three years from 1 April 1991 instead of the then five-year cycle. During preparation the Jakarta and Tangerang governments also agreed to let their water utilities retain and reinvest their share of profits, and PDAM Jaya agreed to permit all households to sell water on to neighbours and distributing water vendors (World Bank, Staff Appraisal Report, 1990). Nothing in the appraisal's agreements requires the utility to be privatised, leased or put under a concession; private-sector participation in municipal services appears only as a policy gap in the Bank's diagnosis.

plantar-minas-gerais.conditions_add: The World Bank's project information document for the Prototype Carbon Fund's Plantar project says the Fund enters into emission reduction purchase agreements with project sponsors "defining the quantity, price and other delivery conditions" together with the monitoring and verification protocols, that "as PCF only buys ERs and agrees a payment schedule against the delivery of certified ER, it does not finance specific project components", and that "payments will only be effected on an annual basis after monitoring and verification". The Fund planned to pay US$5.3 million for reductions bought from 2002 through 2008. To qualify, "the planting area of the Project will have to be defined at least one year before the actual planting" and the plan had to prove that the land had been pasture land since December 1989, and the document states that "the environmental due diligence of the plantation activities have to be guaranteed before plantation, which includes FSC certification" (World Bank, Project Information Document, PCF Minas Gerais Plantar Project, 2002).

kpone-landfill-tema.conditions_add: The credit set conditions before work could start on the waste sites. Before constructing the sanitary landfills at Kwabenya and Tema, or improving the use of, closing and rehabilitating the refuse dumps at Mallam, Oblogo, Kpone and Essipon, the ministry had to "prepare, and thereafter implement, a satisfactory Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) according to the Resettlement Policy Framework" and "acquire all the necessary land", and the appraisal states that "the acquisition of land for the sanitary landfills is a condition of disbursement". The same works also required a satisfactory Environmental Management Plan beforehand. The credit could not take effect until an external auditor had been appointed and a satisfactory Project Implementation Manual adopted, and no later than 30 November 2004 the ministry had to appoint the key project staff, including a project manager, project engineer, training specialist and project accountant (World Bank, Project Appraisal Document, 2004).

why.safeguard: "prepare, and thereafter implement, a satisfactory Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) according to the Resettlement Policy Framework"

Bihar also had to set up a Dam Review Panel by 31 December 1982 with qualifications and terms of reference acceptable to IDA and have the dams inspected periodically after construction, establish a Subernarekha Project Unit, a Subernarekha Research Cell and a Planning and Monitoring Cell by the same date, carry out a pollution control and monitoring programme on terms agreed by IDA by 31 December 1983, and "deny supply of water from project facilities to any industry without the necessary clearance" (World Bank, Staff Appraisal Report, India - Subernarekha Irrigation Project, 1982).

jawa-1-lng-power-fishers.conditions_add: ADB's Report and Recommendation of the President for the Jawa-1 project sets out obligations the borrower and sponsors took on. The borrower was to submit quarterly unaudited and annual audited financial statements together with environmental and social monitoring reports, and to report regularly to ADB on labour measures and periodically on gender measures. "The sponsors will recruit experienced safeguards staff to ensure effective implementation", and on noise the sponsor "has agreed to implement mitigation measures" including pre-boring of piles, "use of dampers when impact piling", "restricting noisy work to daytime hours" and a noise wall (ADB, Report and Recommendation of the President, 2018). The report also describes, as the project's own plans rather than as stated conditions, an environmental and social management plan, a resettlement plan "to guide the negotiations for land acquisition through a willing seller-willing buyer approach", a community grievance mechanism already developed, and mitigation of the clearance of 0.33 hectares of mangroves "by the protection and restoration of remnant coastal vegetation to achieve no net loss in biodiversity".

bhabadah-waterlogging-kjdrp.conditions_add: ADB's evaluation of the loan records that "Forty of the 43 loan covenants were fully or partially complied with" and quotes three special loan covenants from Schedule 6 of the Report and Recommendation of the President: "the Borrower shall coordinate the project activities at the divisional and district levels" through meetings chaired by the commissioner, that before shrimp culture in a polder area "the Borrower shall ensure, or cause to be ensured, that at least 90% of the farmers in such polder area agree", and "to implement, operate, and maintain the Project in a manner consistent with the Borrower's environmental standards".
